mainTopic: The four-מיל rules, a לגיון's scalps, when a flayed hide still counts as connected to the meat for טומאה, and a garment torn through most of it
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of rules that use the measure of four מיל. איבו said it, there were four rules, and one of them is tanning hides. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that you travel four מיל for a מנין or water only going forward. Going backward, you return only if it is less than a מיל. A ברייתא says a house becomes טמא when a soldier from a traveling לגיון enters it, because armies carry human scalps. Then a new משנה teaches how long a hide being flayed still counts as connected to the meat for טומאה. That depends on whether it is being made into a carpet or a jug, or is flayed from the legs, and there is a מחלוקת about the neck skin. The גמרא asks about hide flayed past the grasping measure. רב says it is טהור, and רבי אסי says the טפח next to the flesh stays טמא. רבי אסי's view survives three challenges. The גמרא then defines the grasping measure as a doubled טפח. Finally, a משנה about a torn garment is limited by רב נחמן to a garment immersed that day, and רבה begins two refutations that continue on the next amud.

steps.title: A different version: איבו said it, and there were four rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the earlier report. The speaker was איבו, and he listed four rules about four מיל, not three. The fourth is the tanning of hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was איבו who said it. He said four rules about it, and one of them is tanning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the statement it just quoted. It names a different speaker and says the list had four rules, not three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier version had three rules about the measure of four מיל, said by רבי אבהו in the name of ריש לקיש. This version says איבו said it and adds a fourth rule: עבודה, the tanning of hides. That rule is the one in our משנה, where hides that were walked on for the time it takes to walk four מיל are treated as tanned.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'working.' Here it means tanning a hide, for example by walking on it.
Four (Aramaic). Here it means four rules.
Of them, from among them.

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the four-מיל list back to our משנה. The tanning rule in the משנה uses the same measure as the other rules in the list.

phrases.english: It was איבו who said it,
and he said four rules about it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the measure of four מיל.

phrases.english: and one of them is tanning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the four-מיל statement from the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four-מיל rules were said by איבו, there are four of them, and tanning hides is one.

steps.title: Four מיל only going forward, not going back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא limits the four-מיל rule. You travel that far for a synagogue or water only if it is ahead of you. If it is behind you, you do not go back even one מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: They only taught this when the place is ahead of him. But if it is behind him, he does not go back even one מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא sets a limit on the rule that a person must go up to four מיל to pray with a מנין or to find water for washing his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four-מיל rule applies only when the synagogue or water is in the direction you are already going. Going backward is a bigger burden, so the distance shrinks a lot. You do not have to return even one מיל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this when...' A phrase that narrows an earlier rule.
Ahead of him, in the direction he is going.
Behind him, so he would have to go back.
A measure of distance, about 2,000 אמות.
Goes back, returns.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
They only taught this when it is ahead of him,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule of going four מיל for prayer and for washing hands.

phrases.english: but if it is behind him –
he does not go back even one מיל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows one of the four-מיל rules from the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You go four מיל only toward a place ahead of you. For a place behind you, you do not go back even one מיל.

steps.title: Learning from the wording: go back less than a מיל
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב reads closely: the exemption covers a full מיל. So if the place is less than a מיל behind you, you must go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said, and we can learn from it: it is a full מיל that he does not go back. But for less than a מיל, he does go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב draws a new rule from the exact words of the previous statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said 'even one מיל, he does not go back.' רב אחא בר יעקב reads this as exact. Only a full מיל is too far, so a shorter distance backward still requires going back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from it.' Here: we can learn a rule from this statement.
'But this...' Used to draw the opposite case from a rule.
Less than a מיל.

steps.whatToRemember: Going forward, you go up to four מיל for a מנין or for water. Going backward, you return only if it is less than one מיל.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר, וּמִינַּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov said, and we can learn from it:
it is a full מיל that he does not go back,
but for less than a מיל, he does go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר, וּמִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the exact wording of step 2 and draws its opposite case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the synagogue or water is less than a מיל behind you, you must go back.

steps.title: A soldier from a traveling לגיון makes a house טמא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when a member of a traveling army enters a house, the house becomes טמא. Every such army carries several human scalps, and a scalp is human skin, which carries טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When a לגיון passing from place to place enters a house, the house is טמא. This is because every single לגיון has several scalps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא connected to the משנה's rule that human skin is טמא like human flesh. It shows that rule in a real-life case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said human skin carries the same טומאה as a dead person's flesh. The ברייתא uses that rule. Soldiers carry human scalps, which are skin from the dead, so when they come into a house under one roof, the house becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A legion, a troop of soldiers (from the Roman army).
Scalps, the skin of the head with its hair.
The house becomes ritually impure.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
a legion passing from place to place,
that enters a house – the house is impure,
for there is no legion at all
that does not have several scalps.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לִיגְיוֹן הָעוֹבֵר מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the משנה's rule that human skin is like flesh.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house that a soldier of a traveling לגיון enters is טמא, since such armies carry human scalps.

steps.title: Don't be surprised: the scalp of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא backs up its claim that armies carry scalps. It points to a known case: the scalp of רבי ישמעאל was placed on the heads of kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not be surprised, for the scalp of רבי ישמעאל was placed on the heads of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers someone who doubts that soldiers would really carry human scalps. It gives a well-known example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might find it hard to believe that every לגיון carries scalps. The ברייתא shows this really happened: even the scalp of a great sage, רבי ישמעאל, ended up on the heads of kings.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not be surprised.
For look, since. It brings evidence.
Placed, resting.

phrases.english: And do not be surprised,
for the scalp of Rabbi Yishmael
was placed on the heads of kings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 4 that armies carry human scalps.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that every לגיון carries human scalps.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The known case of רבי ישמעאל's scalp, which was placed on the heads of kings.

steps.title: New משנה: someone who flays an animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It describes a person flaying any kind of animal: a domestic or wild animal, a טהור or טמא one, a small or large one. The next step gives the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who flays a domestic animal or a wild animal, a טהורה one or a טמאה one, a small one or a large one –
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. So far it only lists the cases, and the ruling comes later, so the משנה is setting up its next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes clear that its coming rule covers every kind of animal. Listing all these pairs shows that the type of animal does not change the law about the skin while it is being flayed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
One who flays, who peels the skin off an animal.
A domestic animal and a wild animal.
A ritually pure animal and an impure one (for example, an unslaughtered carcass).
A small animal (like a sheep) and a large animal (like cattle).

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who flays a domestic animal or a wild animal,
a pure one or an impure one,
a small one or a large one –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous discussion and opens a new משנה about flaying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה sets up a case of flaying that covers every kind of animal. The ruling comes in step 7.

steps.title: Carpet and jug: how far the hide stays attached
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the rule for two purposes of flaying. For a carpet, the hide counts as attached for the measure of grasping. For a leather jug, it counts as attached until the breast is flayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is flaying it to make a carpet, the hide counts as attached for the measure of grasping. If he is flaying it to make a jug, it counts as attached until he flays the breast.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the ruling for the flaying case that began in step 6. How long the hide counts as part of the meat depends on what the person plans to make from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a carpet, the animal is cut open along its length and peeled from both sides. The peeled hide keeps counting as attached only until the grasping measure (two טפחים) has been flayed. For a jug, the hide is peeled downward from the neck in one piece. So it counts as attached until the whole breast is flayed.

keyTerms.meaning: A spread-out hide used as a carpet or cover
The measure of grasping, about two טפחים
A leather jug or water-skin
The animal's breast or chest

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the hide is טמא. The question is whether it still counts as joined to the meat, so that טומאה can pass between the hide and the meat.

phrases.english: For a carpet: the measure of grasping.
phrases.notes: The words 'it counts as attached' are left out but assumed. They carry over from the case that started in step 6.

phrases.english: And for a jug: until he flays the breast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the flaying case that step 6 set up
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carpet: the hide stays attached for the grasping measure. Jug: it stays attached until the breast is flayed.

steps.title: Flaying from the legs keeps the whole hide attached
steps.stepSummary: If the flaying starts from the legs, the entire hide counts as connected to the meat. This applies both for receiving טומאה and for passing it on.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who flays starting from the legs: the whole hide counts as connected for טומאה, both to become טמא and to make other things טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a third way of flaying: starting from the legs. Here the entire hide stays connected to the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the hide is peeled up from the legs, it stays in one piece and keeps hanging onto the animal until the very end. So all of it counts as attached. It works both ways: touching the hide can make the meat טמא, and the meat can make the hide טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: One who flays starting from the legs (רגלים)
Counted as connected for the rules of טומאה
To become טמא and to make other things טמא

phrases.english: One who flays from the legs: all of it is a connection for impurity,
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means the whole hide, however much has already been peeled.

phrases.english: to become impure and to make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third method of flaying, with the widest connection
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flaying from the legs: the entire hide is connected for receiving and passing on טומאה.

steps.title: Dispute over the skin left on the neck
steps.stepSummary: Suppose only the skin over the neck is left. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says it no longer counts as connected. חכמים say it stays connected until the whole hide is removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The skin on the neck: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says it is not a connection. חכמים say it is a connection until he flays all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about one last piece: the skin around the neck when everything else is already off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that once nearly everything is off, the leftover neck skin no longer joins the hide to the meat. חכמים hold that as long as any part is still attached, the whole hide stays connected.

keyTerms.meaning: Neck
It does not count as connected

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule changes with the method of flaying. Carpet: only the grasping measure. Jug: until the breast. From the legs: the whole hide. On the last bit of neck skin, there is a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: The skin that is on the neck:
phrases.notes: The case is that everything else has been flayed and only the neck skin is still attached.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: It is not a connection,
and the Rabbis say: It is a connection
until he flays all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹר שֶׁעַל הַצַּוָּאר – רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a dispute about the final stage of flaying
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: the neck skin is not connected. חכמים: it is connected until the hide is fully removed.

steps.title: What about the hide past the grasping measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking about the carpet case. What is the status of the hide beyond the grasping measure?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From here onward, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with a clarifying question about the carpet rule. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the carpet hide counts as attached for the grasping measure. It did not say what happens to the hide beyond that measure. The גמרא wants to know whether that part is fully separate or has some other status.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From this point onward

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From here onward, what?
phrases.notes: 'Here' points back to the grasping measure in the carpet case. He means the part of the hide past that measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by questioning the carpet clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of the hide beyond the grasping measure in the carpet case

steps.title: רב: All flayed hide is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב answers the question: once hide is flayed past the grasping measure, the flayed part is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: The part that has been flayed is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer to the question from step 10. Any hide that has already been peeled off is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hide counts as connected to the meat only while it serves the meat. Once a section is flayed past the grasping measure, רב holds it no longer serves the meat at all. So it neither receives טומאה nor passes it on.

keyTerms.meaning: The part of the hide that has already been flayed (peeled off)
Pure; here, not counted as part of the meat for טומאה

phrases.english: Rav said: The flayed part is pure,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All hide flayed beyond the grasping measure is טהור.

steps.title: רבי אסי: The handbreadth next to the flesh stays impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי disagrees: the טפח of flayed hide closest to the meat is still טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי says: The handbreadth that is next to the flesh is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives a different answer. One טפח of the peeled hide, right where it meets the meat, still counts as connected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the person flays, he holds onto the טפח of hide closest to the meat. That makes it act like a handle for the meat, so it stays connected. This is the opinion the גמרא will now test.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a basic unit of measure
Next to the flesh, the part of the flayed hide closest to the meat
Impure; here, still counted as connected to the meat for טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אסי is not talking about the hide still stuck to the meat. Everyone agrees that hide is connected. He means the first טפח of the hide that has already been peeled back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
A handbreadth that is next to the flesh is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר: טֶפַח הַסָּמוּךְ לַבָּשָׂר טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's answer in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טפח of flayed hide next to the meat is still טמא, and the rest is טהור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טפח next to the flesh is טמא.

steps.title: First challenge: Touching the flayed hide leaves one pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that past the measure, anyone who touches the flayed hide is טהור. That seems to include the טפח next to the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who flays this measure, from then on, one who touches the flayed hide is pure. Doesn't that include even the handbreadth next to the flesh?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אסי from a ברייתא. It teaches that after a certain amount is flayed, touching the flayed hide does not make you טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks about the flayed hide with no exceptions. If it means all of it, then even the טפח next to the flesh is טהור, against רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: This measure, a set amount of flaying
One who touches
Is it not so that…? A setup for a challenge

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who flays this measure,
phrases.notes: This is about an animal that died without שחיטה, after he has peeled off a set amount of hide.

phrases.english: from then on, one who touches the flayed part is pure.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו אֲפִילּוּ בְּטֶפַח הַסָּמוּךְ לַבָּשָׂר?
phrases.english: Is it not even the handbreadth next to the flesh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אסי's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's ruling that the טפח next to the flesh is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls all flayed hide טהור with no exception, so the טפח should be included.

steps.title: Answer: Except for the handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the flayed hide other than the טפח next to the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means everything except the handbreadth next to the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אסי. It says the ברייתא's ruling covers only the flayed hide beyond that first טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not clearly include the טפח, so it can be read as leaving it out. That way it fits רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside of, except for

phrases.english: No, it means apart from the handbreadth next to the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls all flayed hide טהור, including the טפח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking only about the flayed hide beyond the טפח next to the flesh.

steps.title: Second challenge: Only the hide opposite the flesh is impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the hide opposite the flesh is טמא. That implies the flayed טפח next to the flesh is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Hide opposite the flesh is impure. So hide opposite the flesh is impure, but the handbreadth next to the flesh is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא against רבי אסי. It draws an inference from its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only the hide opposite the flesh, meaning still lying on the meat, as טמא. That suggests nothing else is טמא. So the peeled-back טפח next to the flesh would be טהור, against רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide opposite the flesh, the hide lying against the meat
But this; introduces an inference from what the text implies

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּעוֹר שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַבָּשָׂר – טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Come and hear: One who touches the hide opposite the flesh is impure.
The hide opposite the flesh is impure,
but the handbreadth next to the flesh is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּעוֹר שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַבָּשָׂר – טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי אסי after the first one was answered in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's ruling that the טפח next to the flesh is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes only the hide opposite the flesh טמא, so the flayed טפח must be טהור.

steps.title: Answer: The handbreadth is called hide opposite the flesh
steps.stepSummary: The תנא includes the whole טפח next to the flesh in the phrase hide opposite the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא calls the whole handbreadth next to the flesh hide opposite the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. The ברייתא's phrase hide opposite the flesh also covers the flayed טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the phrase means only hide still lying on the meat. The answer widens the phrase to include the טפח closest to the meat. So the ברייתא actually agrees with רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: He calls it
The whole, all of

phrases.english: The תנא: the whole handbreadth next to the flesh,
he calls it hide opposite the flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כׇּל טֶפַח הַסָּמוּךְ לַבָּשָׂר, עוֹר שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַבָּשָׂר קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hide opposite the flesh means only hide still lying on the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase includes the flayed טפח next to the flesh, so that טפח is טמא.

steps.title: Third challenge: The handbreadth next to the flesh is pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about flaying for a carpet says outright that the טפח next to the flesh is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who flays a domestic or wild animal, a pure or impure one, a small or large one, for a carpet, the measure is grasping, and the handbreadth next to the flesh is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא. This one seems to state openly, against רבי אסי, that the טפח next to the flesh is טהור. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first two sources, this one names the טפח next to the flesh directly and calls it טהור. So it cannot be answered by saying the טפח is left out or by redefining a term, as the גמרא did with the earlier sources. It seems to contradict רבי אסי head-on.

keyTerms.meaning: A carpet or spread, a reason for flaying
The measure of grasping, enough hide to hold
Small animal and large animal

phrases.english: Come and hear: One who flays a domestic animal or a wild animal,
a pure one or an impure one, a small one or a large one,
for a carpet, the measure is grasping,
and the handbreadth next to the flesh is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, stronger challenge to רבי אסי after step 16 answered the second.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's ruling that the טפח next to the flesh is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly calls the טפח next to the flesh טהור.

steps.title: The carpet ברייתא is about the first handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the carpet ברייתא, which calls the טפח next to the flesh טהור, is talking about the first טפח flayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? With the first handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 17 by limiting that ברייתא to one specific situation: when only the first טפח has been flayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At that early point, the person flaying does not hold the טפח next to the flesh, so it is not working as a handle for the meat. That is why it is טהור there. Later, once more hide is off, he does grip that טפח, so it does pass on טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrowing answer)
The first handbreadth

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With the first handbreadth.
phrases.notes: He means the very first טפח flayed beyond the grip measure, when hardly any hide is off yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls the טפח next to the flesh טהור in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is טהור only when just the first טפח has been flayed, because then it is not used as a handle.

steps.title: How big is the measure of grasping? One handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines כדי אחיזה, the measure of grasping from the משנה, as one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: How much is the measure of grasping? A handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us the size of כדי אחיזה mentioned in the משנה. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the hide counts like the flesh until enough is flayed to grab onto. Here a ברייתא gives that amount a number: one טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough to grasp; the measure of hide needed to get a grip
How much?

phrases.english: It was taught: How much is the measure of grasping?
A handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: defining a term from the משנה

steps.title: Another ברייתא says two handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with another ברייתא that gives the measure as two טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: two handbreadths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא says the measure of grasping is two טפחים, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources seem to clash on a number. One says one טפח and the other says two, so the גמרא needs to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it...? (opens a challenge)
Two handbreadths

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: two handbreadths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that says כדי אחיזה is one טפח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא gives a different number, two טפחים.

steps.title: אביי: a doubled handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'one טפח' means a doubled טפח, which is two טפחים folded over, so both sources agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A doubled handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the clash: the first ברייתא means a טפח folded double, which is really two טפחים of hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You flay two טפחים, fold them over, and grab them as one doubled טפח. So the ברייתא that says 'one' counts the folded grip, and the one that says 'two' counts the hide itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubled, folded over
A doubled handbreadth, two טפחים folded into one

phrases.english: Abaye said: a doubled handbreadth.
phrases.notes: Picture two טפחים of hide folded over so you hold them as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciling the two sources (both mean the same amount)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One source says one טפח and the other says two, so they disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One טפח' means two טפחים folded double, so they agree.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states outright that the measure of grasping is a doubled טפח, which supports אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught so: How much is the measure of grasping? A doubled handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses אביי's exact words, showing his answer is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer is not just a clever guess. A source actually says 'a doubled טפח,' which confirms it.

keyTerms.meaning: Also like this (introduces support for what was just said)

steps.whatToRemember: כדי אחיזה = a doubled טפח, which is two טפחים of hide folded over and held as one.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
How much is the measure of grasping?
A doubled handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 21
steps.raayaObject: אביי's explanation that כדי אחיזה is a doubled טפח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says 'טפח כפול' outright

steps.title: A garment torn through most of it becomes טהור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה elsewhere: a טמא garment that is torn through most of it no longer counts as connected and is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: A garment that one began to tear, once most of it is torn, it is no longer a connection, and it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new, related topic by quoting a משנה about a טלית being torn. This sets up a discussion that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the half-flayed hide, this is about when something partly separated still counts as one piece. Once most of the garment is torn, the two parts stop counting as connected, so it is no longer a usable garment and loses its טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in a different place in the משנה
A garment or cloak
To tear it
Most of it
A connection; the parts count as one item
Pure, free of טומאה

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת כלים, about a garment that was טמא.

phrases.english: A garment that one began to tear,
once most of it is torn,
it is no longer a connection, and it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: טַלִּית שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ לְקוֹרְעָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about partial separation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא garment torn through most of it is no longer connected and becomes טהור.

steps.title: רב נחמן limits the rule to a garment immersed that day
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the משנה's rule that tearing most of a garment makes it טהור applies only to a garment that is טבולת יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: They only taught this about a garment that was immersed that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in and narrows the משנה from step 23. Its rule about tearing most of a garment only works in one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבולת יום garment has already been dunked in a מקוה, but its purity is not complete until nightfall. רב נחמן says that only for this kind of garment is tearing most of it enough to make it טהור. The phrase לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא tells us he is limiting the משנה, not arguing with it.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of; a phrase that limits a source to a narrower case
Something immersed in a מקוה today whose purity is complete only at nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the משנה is wrong. He is only saying which case it is talking about.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
They taught this only
regarding a garment that was immersed that day.
phrases.notes: The garment was already dunked in a מקוה today, but it isn't fully טהור until nightfall.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּטַלִּית טְבוּלַת יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה quoted in step 23 to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tearing most of a garment makes it טהור only when the garment is טבולת יום.

steps.title: The reason: whoever dunked it will also tear most of it
steps.stepSummary: The reasoning behind רב נחמן's limitation is explained. A person who did not mind dunking the garment will not mind tearing most of it. For any other garment, there is a גזרה because the owner might not really tear most of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he did not spare the garment and immersed it, he will also not spare it, and he will tear most of it. But a garment not immersed that day does not get this rule. That is a decree, in case he does not actually tear most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule is limited to a garment immersed that day. It uses a מיגו: someone who already showed he does not protect the garment will tear it properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that an owner who wants to save his garment will tear only about half and call it 'most'. If he already dunked it, which can harm the cloth, he has shown he is not protecting it, so we trust he tore most of it. For any other garment the חכמים made a גזרה that tearing most is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; a reasoning that says because he did one thing, we can assume he does the other
To spare, to have pity on, to protect
A protective decree made by the חכמים
Most of it

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole basis of the limitation, so it is exactly what רבה is about to attack.

phrases.english: For since he did not spare it
and immersed it,
phrases.notes: Dunking cloth in water can harm it, so he has shown he isn't protective of the garment.

phrases.english: he will not spare it
and he will tear most of it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל טַלִּית שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְבוּלַת יוֹם – לָא,
phrases.english: But a garment that was not immersed that day: no,
it is a decree, lest
he not come to tear most of it.
phrases.notes: The fear is that he'll tear only about half to save the garment, and treat that as 'most'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the limitation in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A same-day-immersed garment is trusted to have been torn through most of it. Other garments fall under a גזרה, so tearing most of them is not enough.

steps.title: רבה's first refutation: people will think same-day immersion is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבה says there are two refutations of רב נחמן's view. The first is that people might mistakenly conclude that an immersion done the same day is already enough. He then starts his second refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There are two refutations of this. One: people might say that an immersion done that same day is effective. And furthermore —
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the limitation from steps 24 and 25. He gives his first objection and then begins a second one, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טבולת יום garment becomes טהור by tearing most of it, onlookers will see it being treated as טהור on the very day it was dunked. They may wrongly conclude that same-day immersion works without waiting for nightfall. So the גזרה should apply here too. The word וְעוֹד sets up the second refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: Refutations, objections
Immersion in a מקוה
Of that same day
Is effective, counts (literally, goes up)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה here is a different sage from רבה בר אבוה quoted in step 24. רבה is the one disagreeing.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
There are two refutations of this matter:
One: lest people say
that an immersion of that same day is effective,
And furthermore:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the limitation and reasoning given in steps 24 and 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's limitation of the משנה to a טבולת יום garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a טבולת יום garment טהור by tearing most of it could lead people to think same-day immersion is enough. So the גזרה should apply to it as well.
